draft.emotion: a neutral observation of size, objective and matter-of-fact
notes: An i-adjective. Unlike 大きな (which can only come directly before a noun, as in 大きな家), 大きい can also be used at the end of a sentence (家が大きい).

senses.definition: Of great physical size, extent, or amount.

examples.text: その犬はとても大きいです。
examples.emotion: impressed by the sheer scale of the dog

senses.definition: Of a sound or voice: high in volume.

examples.text: テレビの音が大きいです。

senses.definition: Significant in scale, degree, or importance.

examples.text: それは大きい問題ですね。

notes: Used for physical size. Unlike 'ookina' (大きな), which is also an adjective used to describe size, 'ookii' can be used as the predicate at the end of a sentence (e.g., 'heya ga ookii').
